mgmt_bio.text: Manuel V. Pangilinan is chairman and chief executive officer of Manila Electric Company (Meralco), where the role is to represent shareholder and stakeholder interests and oversee the board's performance. He graduated cum laude from Ateneo de Manila University with a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and earned an MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. Early in his career he worked for Philippine Investment Management Consultants (PHINMA) in Manila and for Bancom International and American Express Bank in Hong Kong, before founding First Pacific in May 1981. He was First Pacific's managing director from 1981 to 1999, then executive chairman until June 2003, after which he became managing director and chief executive officer.

sentences.quote: Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) was honored with a Four-Golden Arrow recognition for outstanding corporate governance at the 2025 Golden Arrow Awards held in Pasay City on October 23, 2025.
sentences.text: On governance, it won a Four-Golden Arrow recognition in October 2025 for ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard performance, after an ASEAN Asset Class award in July 2025; board policy sets regular cash dividends at 50 percent of consolidated core earnings, with scope for specials.

mgmt_team_view.text: Under chairman and CEO Manuel Velez Pangilinan, Meralco's 2025 core net income rose to a record 50.6 billion pesos from 45.1 billion, meeting its profit target. Capital allocation has turned expansionary: capex surged 144 percent to 108.96 billion pesos as the company expanded power plants and networks, funded largely by a 143 percent jump in borrowings to about 230 billion pesos, with 73 percent allocated to MGen's 3,500-megawatt MTerra Solar and other renewable plants. On governance, it won a Four-Golden Arrow recognition in October 2025 for ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard performance, after an ASEAN Asset Class award in July 2025; board policy sets regular cash dividends at 50 percent of consolidated core earnings, with scope for specials.

The MTerra Solar project, covering 3,500 hectares in Nueva Ecija and Bulacan with 3,500 MWp of solar and 4,500 MWh of storage, began delivering, with Phase 1 inaugurated in July 2026 for 600 MW and 250 MW under Phase 2 targeted for 2027.

sentences.quote: The 15-year contracts will provide 600 MW beginning 26 February 2031, followed by another 300 MW starting 26 February 2032, subject to approval by the Energy Regulatory Commission.

Key risks include regulatory uncertainty and tariff reset delays and demand softness from weather, rooftop solar adoption and economic conditions.
